QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_5

question.text: An investor in Kaveri Macro Fund has NAV INR 120 per unit with HWM at INR 115. She redeems 40% of her units. After redemption, what is the HWM applied to her remaining 60% units for next-period performance-fee crystallisation?

answer.text: Remains at INR 115 (partial redemption does not reset HWM on retained units)
Weighted average of INR 115 and INR 120 based on redemption ratio

explanation.text: The Logic: Under industry practice for performance-fee crystallisation, a partial redemption triggers a performance-fee charge on the redeemed units only (fee on the 120 - 115 = 5 gain per redeemed unit). The HWM on the units the investor continues to hold is NOT reset; the retained 60% units carry forward HWM = 115, and the next crystallisation uses that HWM versus a fresh NAV. This preserves fairness between redeeming and continuing positions. The Trap: Option A wrongly assumes any fee-crystallisation event resets the HWM on retained units (it only resets on the redeemed slice). Option B confuses HWM with cost basis. Option D invents a weighted-average mechanic that no standard PPM uses. Note: The no-reset rule for retained units after a partial redemption and the series/equalisation ledger mechanics are not explicitly stated in the cited XIX-E (Category III AIF Managers) workbook pages, which support HWM and performance-fee disclosure concepts generally. The explanation above reflects general industry/regulatory practice for HWM administration in Category III AIFs.
